name: Endogenous Ecological–Reproductive Closure: Ecological Trace & Selective Memory
scientific_question: Can an evolving process create material ecological information, adapt its use in changing unseen contexts, and gate transfer of internal states among descendants, without a preprogrammed visited-map/copying/reward module?

original_hypotheses.claim: Ecological read/write traces become beneficial on unseen obstacles but maladaptive under unreliable or renewed resources; reliability-sensitive modulation may be favoured.
original_hypotheses.falsifier: Preinstalled fixed slime aversion, passive gradient or inert residue accounts for all benefits after matched material cost.

original_hypotheses.claim: Selectively partitioning learned internal state to descendants sometimes outperforms full copy and full erasure under environmental contingency reversal.
original_hypotheses.falsifier: Neither selective gate nor its causal rescue changes independent daughter-lineage function relative to matched replication controls.

original_hypotheses.claim: Temporal stimulus association can become useful for resource/viability outcomes beyond its original stimulus modalities.
original_hypotheses.falsifier: Stimulus-based contraction response disappears under a held-out ecological outcome, or is fully explained by sensitization/fatigue.
